questions.question: Who is a famous Kuchipudi Dancer to receive Padma Shri in 2001?
questions.solution:
Sobha Naidu was one of the foremost exponents of Kuchipudi dance and a disciple of the legendary Vempati Chinna Satyam.
  • Achievement: She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2001 for her contribution to the classical dance form.
  • Style: She was particularly famous for her portrayal of Satyabhama and Padmavati in dance dramas.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the famous International Sand Art Festival organised, where artists get enthralled by the diverse thoughts and their elucidation on sand?
questions.solution:
The International Sand Art Festival is held annually at Chandrabhaga Beach, Konark, in the state of Odisha.
  • Nature: It showcases the incredible talent of world-class sand artists who create intricate sculptures based on specific themes.
  • Context: It is usually held concurrently with the Konark Dance Festival in December.

questions.question: Select the correct combination of famous palaces and their locations in Rajasthan.
questions.solution:
The Lalgarh Palace is located in Bikaner, Rajasthan. Here is the correction for the other options:
  • Umaid Bhawan Palace is in Jodhpur.
  • Rambagh Palace is in Jaipur.
  • Taj Lake Palace is in Udaipur.

questions.question: Which famous medieval singer was born in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the year 1506?
questions.solution:
Tansen (born Ramtanu Pande) was born in Gwalior in 1506 and became one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar.
  • Musical Style: He is a central figure in Hindustani Classical Music and was a disciple of Swami Haridas.
  • Legacy: He is credited with creating many new Ragas like Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi.

questions.question: The famous Jain temple of Dilwara, built by Solanki rulers, is located at which place?
questions.solution:
The Dilwara Temples are a group of five marble Jain temples located near Mount Abu, Rajasthan.
  • Patronage: They were built between the 11th and 13th centuries by the ministers of the Solanki rulers of Gujarat.
  • Architecture: They are world-famous for their extraordinary marble carvings and intricate ceiling designs.

questions.question: Padma Shri Pandit Rajeev Tharanath, the famous ________________ player is from the state of Karnataka.
questions.solution:
Pandit Rajeev Tharanath is a globally acclaimed Sarod player and a disciple of the legendary Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.
  • Background: He hails from Karnataka and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2019.
  • Instrument: The Sarod is a stringed instrument used primarily in Hindustani music, known for its deep, introspective sound.

questions.question: In 1974, classical singer Naina Devi was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to which of the following singing styles?
questions.solution:
Naina Devi was an eminent classical singer who specialized in the Thumri style of Hindustani music.
  • Background: Though born into an aristocratic family, she dedicated her life to the revival and preservation of semi-classical forms like Thumri, Dadra, and Ghazal.
  • Award: She received the Padma Shri in 1974.

questions.question: Where was the Hindustani classical singer Kumar Gandharva born?
questions.solution:
Kumar Gandharva (born Shivaputra Siddharamayya Komkalimath) was a legendary Hindustani classical singer born in Sulebhavi, Karnataka.
  • Innovation: He is famous for his refusal to be bound by the tradition of any single Gharana and for his unique interpretations of Nirguni Bhajans (Kabir).
  • Note: He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and the Kalidas Samman.

questions.question: Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic singer born in Sankaraguptam village of which state?
questions.solution:
Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was a child prodigy and a giant of Carnatic music, born in the East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh.
  • Versatility: He was not only a vocalist but also a skilled player of the viola, violin, and mridangam.
  • Creation: He created many new Ragas such as Mahati, Lavangi, and Ganapathi.

questions.question: In 2017, who became the first Indian singer to make it to Delhi's Madame Tussauds Museum?
questions.solution:
In 2017, Shreya Ghoshal became the first Indian singer to have her wax statue installed at Madame Tussauds Museum (initially at the Delhi location).
  • Career: She gained national fame after winning the reality show Sa Re Ga Ma Pa and debuted in Bollywood with the film Devdas.

questions.question: In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, which playback singer was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history?
questions.solution:
Lata Mangeshkar, known as the 'Nightingale of India', was listed in the Guinness Book of World Records in 1974 as the most recorded artist.
  • Legacy: She recorded songs in over 36 Indian and foreign languages.
  • Honors: She was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.question: The Hindu temples ‘Hinglaj Mata’ and ‘Katasraj’ are located in which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The Hinglaj Mata (a Shakti Peetha) and Katasraj (an ancient Shiva temple complex) are located in Pakistan.
  • Hinglaj Mata: Located in Balochistan, it is a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus.
  • Katasraj: Located in the Punjab province, it is believed to be the site where the Pandavas lived during their exile.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Bhadaravi Poonam Mela organised every year in the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra?
questions.solution:
The Bhadaravi Poonam Mela is a major religious fair organized in Gujarat.
  • Context: While the famous Ambaji Bhadarvi Poonam is well-known, local melas (fairs) like the one at Nilkanth Mahadev temple in Babra are integral to the cultural fabric of the state.

questions.question: The Kamakshi Saunsthan temple of Goa is crowned with the ________ two-storied tower and with a golden Kalash perched on its Shikhar.
questions.solution:
The Kamakshi Saunsthan temple in Shiroda, Goa, features a unique octagonal (eight-sided) two-storied tower.
  • Architecture: Goan temple architecture often blends local styles with outside influences, seen here in the Shikhara crowned with a golden Kalash.

questions.question: Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri recipient, is an exponent of ________.
questions.solution:
Shovana Narayan is a highly recognized Kathak dancer and a disciple of Birju Maharaj.
  • Recognition: She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1992.
  • Dual Career: Remarkably, she served as a senior officer in the Indian Audit and Accounts Service while maintaining her career as a world-class dancer.

questions.question: Which of the following institutes/projects is declared as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity by UNESCO in May 2001?
questions.solution:
Kuttiyattam (or Koodiyattam), a form of Sanskrit theatre from Kerala, was proclaimed a masterpiece by UNESCO in 2001.
  • Nature: It is one of the oldest living theatrical traditions in India, performed in temple theaters called Koothambalams.
  • Support: The 'National Project to support Kuttiyattam' was launched to ensure its survival.

questions.question: ‘Once a Dancer’ is the autobiography of ________________.
questions.solution:
Allegra Kent is an American ballet dancer who wrote the autobiography titled 'Once a Dancer'.
  • Context: She was a muse to the famous choreographer George Balanchine and was a principal dancer with the New York City Ballet.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities from the Carnatic Music correctly represent the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music'?
questions.option_2: Manambuchavadi Venkatasubbayyar, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar
questions.option_3: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri
questions.option_4: MS Subbalakshmi, DK Pattammal and ML Vasanthakumari
questions.solution:
The 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' refers to three seminal composers of the 18th century: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri.
  • Significance: They revolutionized Carnatic music by creating a vast repertoire of Kritis (compositions) that defined the modern musical system.
  • Origin: All three were born in the town of Thiruvarur in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Sangeet Natak Akademi is/are true?

1. The Sangeet Natak Akademi has been functioning as the apex body of the performing arts in the country.

2. The main objective of the Akademi is to coordinate and collaborate with the government and performing artists.

3. The Sangeet Natak Akademi comes under the Ministry of Culture of the government of India.
questions.solution:
The Sangeet Natak Akademi is the apex body for performing arts in India. All three statements provided are true:
  1. It functions as the premier national academy for music, dance, and drama.
  2. It works to coordinate and collaborate with various artists and organizations.
  3. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture.

questions.question: Where is the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival organised every year?
questions.solution:
The Kala Ghoda Arts Festival is a prominent multicultural festival held annually in Mumbai.
  • Venue: It takes place in the Kala Ghoda precinct (South Mumbai), known for its many museums and art galleries.
  • Scope: It covers a wide range of arts including visual arts, dance, music, theater, and cinema.

questions.question: On which of the following days is National Integration Day observed?
questions.solution:
National Integration Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 19 November in India.
  • Reason: It marks the birth anniversary of Indira Gandhi, the first female Prime Minister of India, to promote love and unity among citizens.
  • Distinction: Note that National Unity Day (31st October) commemorates Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.question: Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are distinguished practitioners of ____________.
questions.solution:
These four legends—Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy, and Anita Ratnam—are all icons of Bharatanatyam.
  • Innovation: Each has contributed uniquely; for example, Padma Subramanyam developed Bharata Nrityam, a style integrating research from temple sculptures.

questions.question: The modern-day __________ was molded by the renowned Tanjore Bandhu, consisting of the four Nattuvanars: Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnayya.
questions.solution:
The Tanjore Bandhu (Tanjore Quartet) consisted of four brothers: Chinnayya, Ponnayya, Sivanandam, and Vadivelu.
  • Impact: They transformed Bharatanatyam from a temple ritual into a concert art form by defining the Margam (the sequence of items in a performance).

questions.question: __________ was the pioneer who modified the Hawaiian slide guitar to play classical ragas.
questions.solution:
Brij Bhushan Kabra was the pioneer who introduced the Hawaiian slide guitar into the world of Indian Classical Music.
  • Modification: He modified the instrument to enable the playing of Meend (glides) and nuances essential for Indian Ragas.
  • Album: He is most famous for the landmark album 'Call of the Valley'.

questions.question: The campaign 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath' is associated with which occasion?
questions.solution:
The 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath' campaign was a massive voluntary cleanliness drive (Shramdaan) organized in 2023.
  • Occasion: It was held as a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti (October 2nd).
  • Motto: The campaign was part of the Swachh Bharat Mission.
